title: How CI/CD Works in 60 Seconds 🚀 #shorts
description:
You push code, and minutes later it's live, without anyone touching a server. That's CI/CD. Continuous integration builds and tests every push automatically and stops the pipeline when a test fails; continuous delivery/deployment packages the passing build and ships it to staging, then production. Tools like GitHub Actions, GitLab CI and Jenkins run it from a config file in your repo.

lines: You push code, and minutes later it's live for millions of users. Nobody touched a server.
Without it, teams merge by hand, test by hand, and deploy late at night, hoping nothing breaks.
CI, continuous integration, means every push triggers a pipeline: your code is built, and the tests run automatically.
If a test fails, the pipeline stops, and you see a red cross, before the bug reaches anyone.
CD, continuous delivery, takes the passing build, packages it, often as a Docker image, and ships it to staging, then production.
Tools like GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, and Jenkins run these pipelines from a simple config file in your repo.
